the number of publications, the number of venues, the number of citations and the number of coauthors all contribute to the popularity of a scholar, but that each of these features alone is insufficient to characterize a scholar popularity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the number and quality of publications, the number and quality (importance) of the co-authors, and the scholar's position in the co-author network, all contribute significantly to the scholar's popularity, and that these features evolve in time in different manners.

the number of publications, the number of venues, and the scholar's importance in the co-author network are positively correlated with scholar popularity, while the rate of publications and the quality of venues are negatively correlated.
the scholar popularity is a function of the number and quality of publications, the number and quality venues where the scholar publishes, and the scholar’s position in the co-authoring network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a scholar's popularity in her field is a function of the number and quality of her publications and the importance of her co-authors.
the scholar popularity is strongly related to the scholar productivity and the scholar impact.
, while the scholar popularity is highly dependent on the scholar productivity, it is also affected by the scholar importance in the co-authoring network.
